pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.48 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum malum sit natura quaedam?
pairs.answer: Unde non potest esse quod malum significet quoddam esse, aut quandam formam seu naturam.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the author's interrogative (utrum...), answered in the Respondeo. Skipped the non-answering preamble (Respondeo dicendum quod unum oppositorum cognoscitur per alterum... Diximus autem supra quod bonum est omne id quod est appetibile... necesse est dicere quod esse et perfectio cuiuscumque naturae rationem habeat bonitatis), which sets up the argument rather than answering. Started at the operative conclusion (Unde non potest esse...) and ended at its full stop; what follows (Relinquitur ergo quod nomine mali significetur quaedam absentia boni...) is further elaboration.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.48 a.2
pairs.question: Utrum malum inveniatur in rebus?
pairs.answer: Unde manifestum est quod in rebus malum invenitur, sicut et corruptio.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the author's interrogative, answered in the Respondeo. Skipped the long preamble on the perfection of the universe (Respondeo dicendum quod... perfectio universi requirit ut sint quaedam quae a bonitate deficere possint... In hoc autem consistit ratio mali, ut scilicet aliquid deficiat a bono), which builds toward the answer. Took the operative concluding sentence introduced by Unde manifestum est..., ending at its full stop; the trailing clause (nam et ipsa corruptio malum quoddam est) is supporting elaboration.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.48 a.3
pairs.question: Utrum malum sit in bono sicut in subiecto?
pairs.answer: Relinquitur ergo quod subiectum mali sit bonum.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the author's interrogative, answered in the Respondeo. Skipped the preamble distinguishing privative vs negative removal of good and establishing that every being in act/potency is a good (Respondeo dicendum quod... malum importat remotionem boni... et similiter omne ens in potentia... bonum quoddam est). Took the final concluding sentence (Relinquitur ergo...), which directly states that the subject of evil is good; it ends the Respondeo at a full stop.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.48 a.4
pairs.question: Utrum malum corrumpat totum bonum?
pairs.answer: Malum non potest totaliter consumere bonum.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the author's interrogative, answered in the Respondeo. The answer is the very first sentence of the Respondeo; dropped the framing Respondeo dicendum quod and capitalized Malum. Ended at the first full stop; what follows (Ad cuius evidentiam, considerandum est quod est triplex bonum...) is the explanatory development.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.48 a.5
pairs.question: Utrum malum sufficienter dividatur per poenam et culpam?
pairs.answer: Sic igitur omne malum in rebus voluntariis consideratum vel est poena vel culpa.
pairs.derivation: Article title is the author's interrogative, answered in the Respondeo. Skipped the preamble distinguishing first/second act and the kinds of evil (Respondeo dicendum quod malum... est privatio boni... Malum igitur quod est per subtractionem formae... habet rationem poenae... Malum autem quod consistit in subtractione debitae operationis... habet rationem culpae). Took the concluding sentence introduced by Sic igitur..., which directly affirms the sufficiency of the division; it ends the Respondeo at a full stop.
